chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: Booker Max Cavelli and Joe Glaser's honesty
summary: Norvo praises booker Max Cavelli as steady and honest, like Joe Glaser, who always gave a straight answer.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So listen, I think we ought to say what we were saying earlier on, just let's mention Max Cavelli, who does do a lot of your bookings, he does book you a lot of places, doesn't he?
He's booking a lot of the jazz guys now.

But Max is steady as a jazz booker and I think the guys respect him for that. When jazz wasn't doing so well, a few years back, he still tried to keep fellas like Charlie Shavers and Roy Eldridge, everybody, tried to keep them working --
In places that would support their talents. God knows they had talent. And, I think they all respected him a little bit for that.
And I think a lot of the agencies that
were so shunted away and went out on different rock bandwagons, with other things, I think the fellas would rather stay with Max, that's just my feeling.
Yeah, Oh, I think it's true.
It's never been said out and out, but I sense it with them.
I mean, you know -- I mean you don't feel, I mean Max isn't it just because he's in it for the business, but I mean, you know he --
He likes it. And he likes the guys he books, he likes to listen to the guys he books.
He is a very nice man.
He has the same quality I always found in Joe Glazer. I always got along with Joe Glazer very well because he never -- he never give anything but a straight answer if I asked him a question.
And we had a great relationship and he was very fond of me, he was fond of the children, which was normal cause he's that way.
All kids, not cause they're mine or anything.
But if I asked Joe a question, directly, and I wanted to know, he would be honest and give me an answer.
I think that's the way it is with Max. I say to him, 'Is this the way it is da-da-da?' And he'll say 'This is the way it is, or I don't know.'
If he doesn't know he doesn't try to say well yeah, it's all right that way or it's not -- you know all around, he gives me a straight answer.
I think musicians like that sort of thing.
I found in being a leader that that's the best way.
No matter what it is, hit it straight.
Yeah. So you know where you stand.
